name: Standards development bodies
one_line: REFUSED. The standards-development record - committee, working draft, ballot, comment resolution, publication, periodic review - is a consensus DOCUMENT-PRODUCTION process, and it evidences no non-exchange party, which is the whole of the nonprofit schema's activation precondition. The material that would distinguish this row cannot activate its own schema; the material that does activate the schema here (a committee roster, a dues notice, a members' ballot) is verbatim the schema's default template. Coverage routes to engineering.standards-library (the standard and its circulated drafts), business_operations.meeting-record and business_operations.board-governance (the body's self-running record, which the nonprofit schema already cedes by name), government.regulatory-rulemaking (a body exercising a delegated rulemaking power), government.education-accreditation (institutional review, which has already claimed that side reciprocally), engineering.product-certification (certifying a named product or management system), engineering.invention-disclosure and legal (IPR and patent-policy declarations), and the nonprofit schema's own default template for the roster and the subscription.
refuse_reason: Fails the node test (CONNECTION section 2) on all three legs, and fails leg 1 in the strongest available way - not 'the same signals as the schema default' but 'signals that cannot activate this schema at all'. (1) DETECTION SIGNALS. The nonprofit schema states its own precondition and calls it the whole schema: every accepted signal must evidence a NON-EXCHANGE relation between two labelled parties - money or labour given without a commensurate return, or service given to a named person who is not paying for it. Sort this row's candidate evidence against that. A working draft, a ballot on a draft, a disposition-of-comments table, a normative-references clause and a designation-plus-edition front matter evidence NO party at all: they are the internal states of a document being written. They are this row's only distinctive evidence and none of it clears the schema's gate, so a row built on them would never fire. The evidence that DOES clear the gate - a committee roster with one row per named member and a membership class, a members' ballot with a notice period and a vote count, a volunteer's unpaid participation, a subscription status - is the schema's MEMBERSHIP-REGISTER default signal, word for word, with the ballot's object changed from the association's own rules to a technical document. Changing what a member votes ON is a value, not a structure. The remaining tempting signal is a standards body's NAME - ISO, IEC, ASTM, IEEE, NFPA, W3C, BSI - and that is constitutionally never-alone; engineering.standards-library already bans it in exactly this world, extending 00's role-ambiguity reasoning: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” (2) DIMENSIONS. The nonprofit schema's prose default is association, then the NON-EXCHANGE COUNTERPARTY OR FUND - the grant, the restricted fund, the appeal, the membership class, the case - then the period, then the document function. A standards-development corpus has no non-exchange counterparty and no fund, so the schema's second and load-bearing level is unfillable. What this corpus actually wants is issuing_body, then standard_designation, with edition carried as metadata - which is engineering.standards-library's researched order, verbatim. Differing from your own schema's default by silently adopting a DIFFERENT schema's default is evidence of being on the wrong schema, not evidence of being a node. (3) PRIVACY RULES. The nonprofit schema's posture is stricter than business_operations for one argued reason: the exposed party is a third party who is neither the user, an employee nor a customer, often disclosed under need or vulnerability - a safeguarded child, a service user. A standards-development record has no such party. Participants are named professionals acting in a declared public capacity, drafts exist in order to be circulated for comment, and the output is published for sale or free download. The posture here is LOOSER than the schema default, which is again an argument for a different schema rather than for a child row. Separately, the hint's own spine - 'committees, working drafts, ballots and comment resolution, publication and review' - is a LIFECYCLE STAGE SEQUENCE over one document type, which the node test names as a disqualifier and which engineering.standards-library has already ruled on: reading a gate word out of 'Draft International Standard' would import the publisher's balloting stage as if it were the holder's design maturity, a fabricated fact. Refusing costs nothing, because every real fixture has a landed home: “Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement.”

deterministic: None authored, and that is the finding rather than an omission. The one structure that is genuinely specific to this world - a disposition-of-comments table with one row per comment carrying a commenter or member body, a clause and line reference, a comment type, a proposed change and a committee disposition - is real, is recognisable, and is recorded here so a later reader can check the refusal rather than take it on trust. It is not written as a signal because it evidences no non-exchange party and therefore cannot activate the nonprofit schema; if it is ever wanted, it belongs beside engineering.standards-library's consensus-process fingerprint, not here.
needs_llm: Nothing is routed here. A standards-shaped file that matches no landed sibling goes to the ordinary bounded model step against whichever schema its structure actually supports - engineering for the document, business_operations for the body's self-running record - and then to a residual home if nothing lands.
never_alone: a standards body's name - ISO, IEC, ASTM, IEEE, SAE, NFPA, W3C, BSI, DIN, ANSI. It appears on the published standard, on the reseller's order confirmation, on a member's dues invoice, in a drawing note, in a certification file and in the footer of an unrelated marketing PDF. True of a tempting false file: ISO-9001-awareness-training-slides.pptx carries the body's name and the word standard on every slide and is business_operations training material.
a designation-shaped token (ISO 27001, ASTM D638, IEEE 802.11, NFPA 70) - it is a citation as often as a subject, and engineering.standards-library owns it when it is the subject.

a stage word - Working Draft, Committee Draft, DIS, FDIS, Public Input, Second Draft. A stage is a value on a document, and reading the publisher's stage as the holder's situation is a fabricated fact.
the words committee, ballot, comment or consensus beside an organisation name. A residents' association, a company change board and a university senate all ballot committees.

grouping_reasons: None authored. A standards-participation corpus does group - one designation across its drafts, ballots, comment tables and published edition, joined by an exact designation plus project or N-number reference - but that group is engineering.standards-library's to reason about, and P9 forms neighbourhoods from evidence regardless of whether this row exists. Nothing here licenses copying a designation read off a published standard onto a bare ballot form that happens to sit beside it.

template.why: Empty because the row is refused, and empty in any case by binding contract - the nonprofit schema declares no field rows under PR-6 and D1's deferral, so no dimension may branch on one (_CONTRACT rules 10 and 15). The emptiness is itself part of the refusal on leg 2: the schema's default order turns on a non-exchange counterparty or a fund, and this corpus has neither, while the order it actually wants - issuing_body then standard_designation, edition as metadata - is already researched and recommended on engineering.standards-library. Not time-first in any case: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.”, and a standard's edition is a content period, never a capture date. Whatever a user does with these files afterwards stays theirs: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

falls_through_to.why: The principal residual for this refused row, because its characteristic isolated file is a downloaded standard, draft or public-input report with no participation evidence around it. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

The honest home for a standalone committee appointment letter, a participation agreement, a patent-policy declaration or a single set of minutes with nothing around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The right home for this world's defining failure - a ballot form, comment table or accreditation packet whose SIDE is unresolved, because a body's copy and a participant's copy are byte-identical. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

Isolated transactional members: a dues invoice, a standard purchase confirmation from a reseller, a meeting registration. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

For the one fixture in this set that names people row by row - a committee roster with affiliations and contact columns. Cautious routing is the cheap error, and no roster may become a folder level named for a person.

sensitivity_why: Recorded at the schema's level rather than argued down, because a refused row must not weaken its parent's posture. The row's own material is unusually PUBLIC - drafts exist to be circulated, ballots are tallied among declared participants, and the output is published - and that looseness is part of leg 3 of the refusal rather than a licence. Two fixtures still carry real exposure: a committee roster is a list of named people with affiliations and often contact columns, and an essential-patent disclosure is commercially sensitive to the declaring organisation. Neither is a nonprofit-family vulnerability - there is no beneficiary, no safeguarded person and no service user anywhere in this world - which is exactly why the family's stricter-than-business_operations posture has nothing to bite on here. The handling class is P7's and is not set.
open_question: Three. (1) NJ-SB-1: the disposition-of-comments table is a genuinely distinctive structure with no landed owner. This refusal routes it to engineering.standards-library on the grounds that it is apparatus of the document rather than of an association, but standards-library's researched signals are about the PUBLISHED artefact - a foreword naming a balloting committee, a normative-references clause - and do not currently name a comment table. Alternatives for R1c: (a) add the comment-table and ballot-record structures to engineering.standards-library's signals, which is this row's recommendation and requires an edit this row did not make; (b) leave them unowned so participant-side files land in Review Later; (c) build a standards-development row on the ENGINEERING schema rather than nonprofit, where the consensus-process fingerprint and the issuing_body-then-designation order already live. Option (c) is the only version of this id that could survive a node test, and it would not be a nonprofit row. (2) NJ-SB-2, reciprocal and already half-written by the neighbour: government.education-accreditation's own open question asks whether it belongs on the government schema at all, since most education accreditors are private membership associations, and it points at THIS id as the alternative home. This row is refused, so that alternative no longer exists. R1c must resolve the neighbour's NJ-1 knowing its named escape hatch is gone - the choices become keep it on government, or split assessor-side review by the reviewer's own public-body status. This row did not edit the neighbour. (3) NJ-SB-3: government.regulatory-rulemaking flags as unresolved whether a delegated standards body or self-regulatory organisation is exercising a delegated rulemaking power or acting as a private association. This refusal removes the private-association branch of that question from the nonprofit side without answering it: where a standards body's output is incorporated by reference into law, the notice-and-comment record is rulemaking-shaped and rulemaking is the better home, but the discriminator - incorporation by reference - is a legal fact the product must not decide. R1c should state whether that branch is simply abstention.
